# Data Source: stripe_issuing_transaction

A capture or refund of money spent with an Issuing card: captures are negative amounts and refunds positive. It lives on a connected account, so read it through a provider configuration whose `stripe_account` is that account. Look one up by its `id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "connected_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "The connected account the object lives on."
}

provider "stripe" {
  alias          = "connected"
  stripe_account = var.connected_account
}

data "stripe_issuing_transaction" "purchase" {
  provider = stripe.connected
  id       = "ipi_1MvSieLkdIwHu7ixdA4EgS3k"
}

output "transaction_amount" {
  value = data.stripe_issuing_transaction.purchase.amount
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the issuing transaction to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `amount` - The transaction amount, which will be reflected in your balance. This amount is in your currency and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal).
* `amount_details` - Detailed breakdown of amount components. These amounts are denominated in `currency` and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). See [`amount_details`](#amount_details) below.
* `authorization` - The `Authorization` object that led to this transaction.
* `balance_transaction` - ID of the [balance transaction](https://docs.stripe.com/api/balance_transactions) associated with this transaction.
* `card` - The card used to make this transaction.
* `cardholder` - The cardholder to whom this transaction belongs.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `dispute` - If you've disputed the transaction, the ID of the dispute.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `merchant_amount` - The amount that the merchant will receive, denominated in `merchant_currency` and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). It will be different from `amount` if the merchant is taking payment in a different currency.
* `merchant_currency` - The currency with which the merchant is taking payment.
* `merchant_data` - See [`merchant_data`](#merchant_data) below.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `network_data` - Details about the transaction, such as processing dates, set by the card network. See [`network_data`](#network_data) below.
* `purchase_details` - Additional purchase information that is optionally provided by the merchant. See [`purchase_details`](#purchase_details) below.
* `token` - [Token](https://docs.stripe.com/api/issuing/tokens/object) object used for this transaction. If a network token was not used for this transaction, this field will be null.
* `treasury` - [Treasury](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury) details related to this transaction if it was created on a [FinancialAccount](/docs/api/treasury/financial_accounts See [`treasury`](#treasury) below.
* `type` - The nature of the transaction. Possible values: `capture`, `refund`.
* `wallet` - The digital wallet used for this transaction. One of `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, or `samsung_pay`. Possible values: `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `samsung_pay`.

<a id="amount_details"></a>
### `amount_details`

The `amount_details` attribute supports:

* `atm_fee` - The fee charged by the ATM for the cash withdrawal.
* `cashback_amount` - The amount of cash requested by the cardholder.

<a id="merchant_data"></a>
### `merchant_data`

The `merchant_data` attribute supports:

* `category` - A categorization of the seller's type of business. See our [merchant categories guide](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/merchant-categories) for a list of possible values.
* `category_code` - The merchant category code for the seller’s business
* `city` - City where the seller is located
* `country` - Country where the seller is located
* `name` - Name of the seller
* `network_id` - Identifier assigned to the seller by the card network. Different card networks may assign different network_id fields to the same merchant.
* `postal_code` - Postal code where the seller is located
* `state` - State where the seller is located
* `tax_id` - The seller's tax identification number. Currently populated for French merchants only.
* `terminal_id` - An ID assigned by the seller to the location of the sale.
* `url` - URL provided by the merchant on a 3DS request

<a id="network_data"></a>
### `network_data`

The `network_data` attribute supports:

* `authorization_code` - A code created by Stripe which is shared with the merchant to validate the authorization. This field will be populated if the authorization message was approved. The code typically starts with the letter "S", followed by a six-digit number. For example, "S498162". Please note that the code is not guaranteed to be unique across authorizations.
* `processing_date` - The date the transaction was processed by the card network. This can be different from the date the seller recorded the transaction depending on when the acquirer submits the transaction to the network.
* `transaction_id` - Unique identifier for the authorization assigned by the card network used to match subsequent messages, disputes, and transactions.

<a id="purchase_details"></a>
### `purchase_details`

The `purchase_details` attribute supports:

* `fleet` - Fleet-specific information for transactions using Fleet cards. See [`purchase_details.fleet`](#purchase_details.fleet) below.
* `flight` - Information about the flight that was purchased with this transaction. See [`purchase_details.flight`](#purchase_details.flight) below.
* `fuel` - Information about fuel that was purchased with this transaction. See [`purchase_details.fuel`](#purchase_details.fuel) below.
* `lodging` - Information about lodging that was purchased with this transaction. See [`purchase_details.lodging`](#purchase_details.lodging) below.
* `receipt` - The line items in the purchase. See [`purchase_details.receipt`](#purchase_details.receipt) below.
* `reference` - A merchant-specific order number.

<a id="purchase_details.fleet"></a>
### `purchase_details.fleet`

The `purchase_details.fleet` attribute supports:

* `cardholder_prompt_data` - Answers to prompts presented to cardholder at point of sale. See [`purchase_details.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data`](#purchase_details.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data) below.
* `purchase_type` - The type of purchase. One of `fuel_purchase`, `non_fuel_purchase`, or `fuel_and_non_fuel_purchase`.
* `reported_breakdown` - More information about the total amount. This information is not guaranteed to be accurate as some merchants may provide unreliable data. See [`purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown`](#purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown) below.
* `service_type` - The type of fuel service. One of `non_fuel_transaction`, `full_service`, or `self_service`.

<a id="purchase_details.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data"></a>
### `purchase_details.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data`

The `purchase_details.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data` attribute supports:

* `driver_id` - Driver ID.
* `odometer` - Odometer reading.
* `unspecified_id` - An alphanumeric ID. This field is used when a vehicle ID, driver ID, or generic ID is entered by the cardholder, but the merchant or card network did not specify the prompt type.
* `user_id` - User ID.
* `vehicle_number` - Vehicle number.

<a id="purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown"></a>
### `purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown`

The `purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown` attribute supports:

* `fuel` - Breakdown of fuel portion of the purchase. See [`purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel`](#purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel) below.
* `non_fuel` - Breakdown of non-fuel portion of the purchase. See [`purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel`](#purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel) below.
* `tax` - Information about tax included in this transaction. See [`purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax`](#purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax) below.

<a id="purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel"></a>
### `purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel`

The `purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel` attribute supports:

* `gross_amount_decimal` - Gross fuel amount that should equal Fuel Volume multiplied by Fuel Unit Cost, inclusive of taxes.

<a id="purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel"></a>
### `purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel`

The `purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel` attribute supports:

* `gross_amount_decimal` - Gross non-fuel amount that should equal the sum of the line items, inclusive of taxes.

<a id="purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax"></a>
### `purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax`

The `purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax` attribute supports:

* `local_amount_decimal` - Amount of state or provincial Sales Tax included in the transaction amount. Null if not reported by merchant or not subject to tax.
* `national_amount_decimal` - Amount of national Sales Tax or VAT included in the transaction amount. Null if not reported by merchant or not subject to tax.

<a id="purchase_details.flight"></a>
### `purchase_details.flight`

The `purchase_details.flight` attribute supports:

* `departure_at` - The time that the flight departed.
* `passenger_name` - The name of the passenger.
* `refundable` - Whether the ticket is refundable.
* `segments` - The legs of the trip. See [`purchase_details.flight.segments`](#purchase_details.flight.segments) below.
* `travel_agency` - The travel agency that issued the ticket.

<a id="purchase_details.flight.segments"></a>
### `purchase_details.flight.segments`

The `purchase_details.flight.segments` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `arrival_airport_code` - The three-letter IATA airport code of the flight's destination.
* `carrier` - The airline carrier code.
* `departure_airport_code` - The three-letter IATA airport code that the flight departed from.
* `flight_number` - The flight number.
* `service_class` - The flight's service class.
* `stopover_allowed` - Whether a stopover is allowed on this flight.

<a id="purchase_details.fuel"></a>
### `purchase_details.fuel`

The `purchase_details.fuel` attribute supports:

* `industry_product_code` - [Conexxus Payment System Product Code](https://www.conexxus.org/conexxus-payment-system-product-codes) identifying the primary fuel product purchased.
* `quantity_decimal` - The quantity of `unit`s of fuel that was dispensed, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places.
* `type` - The type of fuel that was purchased. One of `diesel`, `unleaded_plus`, `unleaded_regular`, `unleaded_super`, or `other`.
* `unit` - The units for `quantity_decimal`. One of `charging_minute`, `imperial_gallon`, `kilogram`, `kilowatt_hour`, `liter`, `pound`, `us_gallon`, or `other`.
* `unit_cost_decimal` - The cost in cents per each unit of fuel, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places.

<a id="purchase_details.lodging"></a>
### `purchase_details.lodging`

The `purchase_details.lodging` attribute supports:

* `check_in_at` - The time of checking into the lodging.
* `nights` - The number of nights stayed at the lodging.

<a id="purchase_details.receipt"></a>
### `purchase_details.receipt`

The `purchase_details.receipt` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `description` - The description of the item. The maximum length of this field is 26 characters.
* `quantity` - The quantity of the item.
* `total` - The total for this line item in cents.
* `unit_cost` - The unit cost of the item in cents.

<a id="treasury"></a>
### `treasury`

The `treasury` attribute supports:

* `received_credit` - The Treasury [ReceivedCredit](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury/received_credits) representing this Issuing transaction if it is a refund
* `received_debit` - The Treasury [ReceivedDebit](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury/received_debits) representing this Issuing transaction if it is a capture
